tasks.title: Create src/components/scholarships/expanded-scholarship.tsx (full modal lifecycle)
tasks.description:
Create a new file at src/components/scholarships/expanded-scholarship.tsx that owns the modal's full lifecycle: AnimatePresence wrapper, backdrop, focus trap (via existing useFocusTrap hook), scroll lock (via existing useScrollLock hook), Escape handling, focus capture/restoration, layoutId shared-element animation, and the dialog body markup.

COMPONENT SIGNATURE:
```ts
"use client"

interface ExpandedScholarshipProps {
  scholarship: Scholarship | null
  onClose: () => void
}

export function ExpandedScholarship({ scholarship, onClose }: ExpandedScholarshipProps): JSX.Element
```

`null` renders nothing meaningful in the AnimatePresence body (no DOM); transitions back to null trigger AnimatePresence's exit animation and `onExitComplete={restorePreviousFocus}`.

LIFT VERBATIM from src/components/scholarships/scholarship-grid.tsx the dialog body markup (currently lines ~367–615 — the AnimatePresence onExitComplete block + backdrop motion.div + modal-wrapper motion.div + dialog content motion.div with all children: tinted header zone, classification badges, title, gradient underline, provider, amount/deadline/openDate row, description body, eligibility section, CTA row with Apply Now / Share buttons). DO NOT change layout, copy, classNames, animation timings, or styling — preserve exactly.

IMPORTS NEEDED (gather from grid):
- `useEffect`, `useRef`, `useCallback`, `useLayoutEffect` from "react".
- `AnimatePresence`, `motion` from "motion/react".
- `Icon` from "@iconify/react".
- `cn` from "@/lib/utils".
- `useFocusTrap` from "@/hooks/use-focus-trap".
- `useScrollLock` from "@/hooks/use-scroll-lock".
- `Button` from "@/components/ui/button/button".
- `CLASSIFICATION_COLORS`, `getClassificationTint`, `type Scholarship` from "@/data/scholarships".

LIFECYCLE IMPLEMENTATION:

1. PREVIOUS FOCUS CAPTURE: declare `const previousFocusRef = useRef<HTMLElement | null>(null)`. Use a `useLayoutEffect` that runs when `scholarship` transitions from null to non-null:
   ```ts
   useLayoutEffect(() => {
     if (scholarship !== null && previousFocusRef.current === null) {
       const active = typeof document !== "undefined" ? (document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null) : null
       previousFocusRef.current = active
     }
   }, [scholarship])
   ```
   useLayoutEffect runs synchronously after DOM updates BEFORE useEffect, so it fires before useFocusTrap moves focus.

2. RESTORE FOCUS: `const restorePreviousFocus = useCallback(() => { ... })` that focuses `previousFocusRef.current` if it has a `.focus` method, then nulls the ref. This is passed to `<AnimatePresence onExitComplete={restorePreviousFocus}>`.

3. SCROLL LOCK: `useScrollLock(scholarship !== null)`.

4. ESCAPE LISTENER: `useEffect` that listens for `keydown` on `window`, calling `onClose()` on Escape. Effect dep array: `[scholarship, onClose]`. Only attach when `scholarship !== null`.

5. FOCUS TRAP: declare `const dialogRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null)`. Pass to motion.div as `ref={dialogRef}`. Call `useFocusTrap(dialogRef, scholarship !== null)`. The hook owns Tab cycling and initial focus on activation. **DELETE the inline onKeyDown Tab handler that currently lives on the dialog motion.div in the grid (~lines 417–432).** The hook subsumes it.

6. The close `<button autoFocus>` (~grid line 461) — KEEP `autoFocus` for now. The PRD says preserve existing behaviour. Note that useFocusTrap also auto-focuses the first focusable on activation; if there's a conflict (close button is the first focusable element via document order), it's idempotent. Leave autoFocus to avoid behavioural drift.

RENDER STRUCTURE:
```tsx
return (
  <AnimatePresence onExitComplete={restorePreviousFocus}>
    {scholarship && (
      <>
        <motion.div key="backdrop" ... onClick={onClose} aria-hidden="true" />
        <motion.div key="modal-wrapper" ... onClick={onClose}>
          <motion.div
            ref={dialogRef}
            data-modal-content
            role="dialog"
            aria-modal="true"
            aria-labelledby="expanded-dialog-title"
            onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
            layoutId={`card-${scholarship.id}`}
            className={...}
          >
            {/* dialog body lifted verbatim from grid */}
          </motion.div>
        </motion.div>
      </>
    )}
  </AnimatePresence>
)
```

IMPORTANT: do NOT touch the source ScholarshipCard's layoutId — the shared-element seam is preserved as-is.

- src/components/scholarships/expanded-scholarship.tsx (NEW file)
acceptance: Component signature: ExpandedScholarship({ scholarship: Scholarship | null, onClose: () => void }): JSX.Element. null renders nothing (no animation, no DOM); AnimatePresence lives inside the component and handles the exit animation when scholarship transitions back to null.

The component owns: AnimatePresence onExitComplete=restorePreviousFocus wrapper; backdrop with onClick=onClose; dialog with role/aria-modal/aria-labelledby/layoutId/onClick stopPropagation; useFocusTrap (replaces inline onKeyDown); useScrollLock(scholarship !== null); Escape useEffect; previousFocusRef + restorePreviousFocus; autoFocus on close button; full dialog body markup.
src/hooks/use-focus-trap.ts is imported instead of re-implementing the Tab handler.
tasks.notes: Self-contained component: AnimatePresence + backdrop + dialog with role/aria-modal/aria-labelledby/layoutId. useFocusTrap(dialogRef, scholarship !== null) replaces the inline Tab onKeyDown handler. useScrollLock(scholarship !== null). Escape useEffect attaches to window. previousFocusRef captured via useLayoutEffect on null→non-null transition (runs before useFocusTrap moves focus). restorePreviousFocus runs in onExitComplete. tasks.title: Add expanded-scholarship.component.test.tsx (8 PRD cases)
tasks.description:
Create src/components/scholarships/__tests__/expanded-scholarship.component.test.tsx with full PRD coverage (8 cases per PRD §Testing Decisions).

PRIOR ART (read first):
- src/hooks/__tests__/use-focus-trap.component.test.tsx — pattern for testing focus-trapped components.
- src/components/scholarships/__tests__/scholarship-card.component.test.tsx — pattern for component tests in this project (mock motion/react, fixture shape, render style).

IMPORTS:
```ts
import { describe, it, expect, vi } from "vitest"
import { render, screen, fireEvent } from "@testing-library/react"
import { ExpandedScholarship } from "../expanded-scholarship"
import type { Scholarship } from "@/data/scholarships"
```

MOCK motion/react if scholarship-card.component.test.tsx mocks it (check that file's mock pattern at the top — typically AnimatePresence is mocked to render children, motion.div to render plain div). Adopt the same mocks.

FIXTURE: a single Scholarship object with realistic fields (use scholarship-card.component.test.tsx's fixture as a template, including eligibilityTags: []).

CASES:

1. it("renders nothing when scholarship is null"):
   - render(<ExpandedScholarship scholarship={null} onClose={() => {}} />).
   - assert document.body or container has no element with role="dialog".

2. it("renders dialog with correct ARIA when scholarship is provided"):
   - render(<ExpandedScholarship scholarship={fixture} onClose={() => {}} />).
   - assert getByRole("dialog") exists.
   - assert role="dialog" + aria-modal="true" + aria-labelledby="expanded-dialog-title".
   - assert the title element has id="expanded-dialog-title".

3. it("calls onClose on Escape key"):
   - const onClose = vi.fn().
   - render with fixture + onClose.
   - fireEvent.keyDown(window, { key: "Escape" }) — or document, depending on what the implementation listens to. Check the new component's escape handler attaches to window.
   - assert onClose was called once.

4. it("calls onClose when backdrop is clicked"):
   - const onClose = vi.fn().
   - render with fixture + onClose.
   - fireEvent.click on the backdrop element. Find it via aria-hidden="true" or a specific data attribute. Easiest: target the parent of the dialog with the dimming class — but querying by aria-hidden is robust.
   - assert onClose was called.

5. it("does not call onClose when dialog body is clicked"):
   - const onClose = vi.fn().
   - render with fixture + onClose.
   - fireEvent.click(getByRole("dialog")).
   - assert onClose was NOT called (the dialog stops propagation).

6. it("focus trap: Tab from last focusable cycles to first"):
   - render with fixture.
   - find focusable elements inside the dialog (close button, Apply Now, Share, etc.).
   - focus the LAST focusable (e.g., Share button).
   - fireEvent.keyDown(document, { key: "Tab" }).
   - assert document.activeElement is now the FIRST focusable (close button).

7. it("focus trap: Shift+Tab from first focusable cycles to last"):
   - same setup.
   - focus the FIRST focusable (close button).
   - fireEvent.keyDown(document, { key: "Tab", shiftKey: true }).
   - assert document.activeElement is now the LAST focusable.

8. it("focuses close button when dialog opens"):
   - render initially with scholarship={null}.
   - rerender with scholarship={fixture}.
   - assert document.activeElement is the close button (aria-label="Close" or query by name).

9. it("restores focus to the previously focused element when dialog closes"):
   - render a wrapper with a focusable trigger button + the dialog.
   - focus the trigger button.
   - rerender with scholarship={fixture}.
   - rerender with scholarship={null} — this triggers AnimatePresence exit, which fires onExitComplete → restorePreviousFocus.
   - NOTE: jsdom may not fire onExitComplete naturally because the mocked AnimatePresence may not trigger lifecycle. If the test infrastructure mocks AnimatePresence to render children directly, restorePreviousFocus won't fire. In that case, the test can verify restorePreviousFocus is wired via direct ref check OR skip with an explanation.
   - PRACTICAL: if onExitComplete is hard to trigger in jsdom, write a simpler version that asserts the component captures previousFocusRef on mount (e.g., via spying on document.activeElement at a known moment, or by accepting this case as a TODO documented in test notes).

If case 9 proves intractable in jsdom (mocked AnimatePresence doesn't fire onExitComplete), it's acceptable to mark it as `it.skip` with a comment explaining the jsdom limitation and verify the same logic exists by reading the component source (the test file's other 8 cases plus a manual smoke covers the user-facing behaviour). Document this decision in the progress.txt note.

With a scholarship, the dialog renders with role="dialog", aria-modal="true", and the title element has the id referenced by aria-labelledby.
Clicking the dialog body does not call onClose.
Tab from the last focusable element in the dialog cycles to the first; Shift+Tab from the first cycles to the last (focus trap).

tasks.notes: 8/9 tests pass; case 9 (focus restoration on close) skipped with documented justification: autoFocus on close button fires during commit-mutation phase BEFORE ExpandedScholarship's useLayoutEffect runs, so previousFocusRef captures the close button instead of the prior trigger. This is a real bug in real browsers, not just jsdom — T04 fixes it. tasks.title: Fix focus-restoration timing: remove autoFocus, rely on useFocusTrap; unskip case 9
tasks.description:
T03 surfaced a real bug: autoFocus on the close button in src/components/scholarships/expanded-scholarship.tsx fires during React's commit-mutation phase BEFORE the component's useLayoutEffect captures previousFocusRef. Result: previousFocusRef captures the close button (already focused) instead of the trigger element, so restorePreviousFocus on close is a no-op.

ROOT CAUSE: autoFocus is a React-managed mutation effect that fires before layout effects. Order: render → DOM mutations (including autoFocus → element.focus()) → useLayoutEffect → useEffect.

FIX: drop autoFocus from the close button. useFocusTrap (called via useEffect inside the hook) auto-focuses the first focusable element on activation. The corrected order is:
  1. Render.
  2. DOM mutations (no autoFocus).
  3. useLayoutEffect in ExpandedScholarship → captures previousFocusRef = whatever was focused (the trigger).
  4. useEffect in useFocusTrap → focuses first focusable (close button).

This matches user-facing behaviour: close button still gets focus on open, AND restorePreviousFocus actually works.

FILE 1: src/components/scholarships/expanded-scholarship.tsx
- Find the close button JSX (the `<button type="button" onClick={handleClose}` or similar with `autoFocus` prop).
- DELETE the `autoFocus` prop. Keep everything else (className, aria-label, onClick, the Icon child).

FILE 2: src/components/scholarships/__tests__/expanded-scholarship.component.test.tsx
- Find the `it.skip("restores focus to previously focused element ...", ...)` block.
- Remove `.skip` so the case runs (`it("restores ...")`).
- Verify the test body matches the spec; the test pattern uses a Wrapper component with a trigger button + state-controlled scholarship. After the fix, focus should land on the trigger button after `lastOnExitComplete()` is invoked.
- If the test still fails after removing autoFocus, debug: confirm useLayoutEffect captures the right element (insert a console.log in test if needed, then remove). Possible remaining gotcha: jsdom may not honor focus management identically to real browsers — if so, document and re-skip with a sharper note.

DO NOT modify other code in either file. DO NOT touch the grid or any other component.

Files you may create/modify (DO NOT touch others):
- src/components/scholarships/expanded-scholarship.tsx
- src/components/scholarships/__tests__/expanded-scholarship.component.test.tsx
acceptance: When the dialog transitions from a scholarship to null, focus is restored to the element that was focused before the dialog opened.
When the dialog opens, the close button receives focus (still satisfied via useFocusTrap).
tasks.notes: Removed autoFocus from close button. useLayoutEffect now captures previousFocusRef BEFORE useFocusTrap's useEffect moves focus to close button. 9/9 tests pass (no skips). Carry-forward principle: never combine autoFocus on a child with a useLayoutEffect capture in the parent — autoFocus wins because it fires during commit-mutation phase. Either capture in parent layout effect + child useEffect for focus move, or capture before the modal mounts.
